---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Intangible Weighted Cash Profitability
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(oancf, at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: Cash profitability is most informative where expensed intangible spending distorts accrual earnings, so the profitability premium should scale continuously with intangible intensity rather than switching on at a threshold.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This directly repairs the gen-0 conditional signal, whose strong FMB slope (3.31) collapsed to zero FF5 alpha because the hard indicator assigned zero to ~70% of firms and produced a degenerate, tie-heavy portfolio sort. Replacing the 0/1 gate with a continuous IND_RANK weight preserves the same interaction (signed profitability amplified by intangible intensity) while restoring a monotone, well-populated cross-sectional spread.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Profit On Capitalized Intangible Stock
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(intan, 0), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: The relevant measure of hidden capital is the accumulated intangible stock (five-year R&D plus booked purchased intangibles), not the single-year spending flow, so profitable firms with the largest hidden stock relative to reported assets are the most understated.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The gen-0 winner used a one-year flow intensity scaled by sales; this isolates the design choice of stock-versus-flow intangible measurement while holding the rank-product structure and profitability leg fixed. Coalescing missing R&D and intangibles to zero should also widen coverage beyond the 0.143 of the winner, testing whether the effect survives outside the intangible-reporting subsample.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Organization Capital Productivity
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(xsga, COALESCE(xad, 0)), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: SG&A and advertising build organization and brand capital that is fully expensed; firms that sustain high operating profitability despite heavy organization-capital spending own productive assets that never appear on the balance sheet.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This changes the intangible channel from R&D (science capital) to selling/brand/organizational capital, a distinct and much broader population than R&D reporters, so it tests whether the mechanism is about innovation specifically or about expensed investment generally. Using oibdp (pre-depreciation operating income) keeps the profitability leg from being mechanically depressed by the same expensing.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Intangible Spend With Rising Profit Path
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at), 3)), IND_RANK(TREND(RATIO(oiadp, at), 5)))
HYPOTHESIS: Intangible investment is "validated" only when the profitability path is improving; sustained heavy spenders whose operating return on assets is trending upward have demonstrated that the invisible capital is productive.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This replaces the level of profitability with its five-year slope, testing whether the market underreacts to the slow accumulation of evidence that intangible outlays are paying off rather than to the static profitability level. It also repairs the gen-0 proposal rejected for lacking a profitability-exclusive variable by using oiadp and xad explicitly.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Fully Capitalized Intangible ROA
EXPRESSION: RATIO(ADD(oiadp, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), ADD(at, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)))
HYPOTHESIS: Restating the income statement and balance sheet as if intangible outlays were investment yields the firm's true return on total (tangible plus intangible) capital; the market prices reported ROA and therefore misprices firms whose adjusted return is much higher.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Unlike gen-0's Return On Intangible Capital, which divided profit only by intangible capital and mechanically ranked low-intangible firms highest (producing a perverse negative alpha), this scales adjusted profit by the full adjusted capital base so the intangible term enters both numerator and denominator consistently. It tests whether the interaction is better expressed as an accounting restatement than as a rank product.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Unvalidated Intangible Buildup
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(DELTA(COALESCE(intan, 0), 1), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(oiadp, 1), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms that rapidly add booked intangible assets (largely acquisition-driven) while their operating profitability deteriorates are capitalizing value that is not being validated by earnings, and should subsequently underperform.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: This is the mirror image of the core story: acquired intangibles overstate rather than understate the productive asset base, so the same profitability-by-intangible interaction should reverse sign when the intangible leg is a purchased-asset increase and the profitability leg is deteriorating. Testing the short side explicitly tells us whether the archive's positive alphas come from the long leg (productive innovators) or the short leg (unvalidated intangible growth).
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
